title: The falsy values you must memorize
why_it_matters: Every if statement in JavaScript depends on this list.
explanation: JavaScript treats a few values as false inside an if: false, 0, an empty string, null, undefined and NaN. Everything else counts as true, including the string '0' and empty arrays or objects.
code:
const falsy = [false, 0, "", null, undefined, NaN];
console.log(falsy.filter(Boolean).length); // 0
console.log(Boolean("0"));                 // true
console.log(Boolean([]));                  // true
try_it: Quiz: is the string 'false' truthy or falsy? Test it with Boolean('false').
